title: Kickoff and Q3 results
gist: Sofia sets the agenda and walks through Q3: on-time delivery up to 93.8% from 90.1%, fuel cost down 8% across 180 vans in three metros; Jordan agrees the numbers are good but flags the Sep 24 outage as the main topic.

turns.t: Hi, hey Jordan, can you hear me okay? I think Teams just did the thing where it switched my mic to the laptop again.
Yeah, I can hear you. You're a little quiet but it's fine.
Okay, hang on, let me — is that better?
Better, yeah.
Great. So Asher's on from our side, and I saw Aisha accepted, so she should be joining.
Hey Jordan. Good to see you.
Hey Asher. Yeah, Aisha's coming, she was out on the floor at the depot when I left, so give her a minute.
No problem at all. While we wait, did you guys survive the heat last week? I saw it was like a hundred and four out there on Thursday.

Oh, don't. We had two vans where the reefer units just gave up, middle of the afternoon, full of dairy. So that was a fun day. Nothing to do with you guys, to be clear, that one's on our maintenance schedule. But yeah. It's been a month.
Oof. Yeah, I believe it.
Hi, sorry, sorry. I'm here. I was literally walking out of the loading bay.

Hey Aisha, perfect timing, we were just talking about your reefer units, so. Okay. So I'll keep the intro short. I put an agenda in the invite, but roughly, I want to start with the Q3 numbers because some of them are genuinely good and I want you to have them. Then the twenty-fourth, which I know is the big one, and Asher's here partly for that. Then roadmap, including live ETA sharing. Then Aisha, I'd love to hear from you about the driver side. And then we save time at the end for Sacramento and for the renewal. Does that work? Anything you'd add?
That works. I'll just be upfront, the twenty-fourth is the thing I most want to talk about, so let's not rush through it to get to the slides.
Totally fair. We won't. I'll go quick on the numbers and then we'll give that the time it needs.
Okay.

So, Q3. On-time delivery across all three metros was ninety-three point eight percent for the quarter. In Q2 it was ninety point one. So that's a bit over three and a half points, which, at your volume, that's a lot of deliveries that landed inside the window that didn't before. Fuel cost is down eight percent quarter over quarter. And that's on the same footprint, a hundred and eighty vans, three metros, so it's not like we got there by adding capacity. Most of that is the stop sequencing changes we made in July, and the time window tightening Aisha's team did on the evening slots. I'll share the deck after, it's got the per-metro breakdown.
Is the eight percent raw fuel spend, or is that normalized? Because diesel was up in August, so if it's raw I'd actually be surprised.

Good question. It's — so it's fuel spend per route, uh, no, sorry, let me correct that. It's gallons per route, so it's volume, not dollars. So diesel prices don't touch it. In dollars it's a bit smaller because of August, I think it's closer to six, but I'll put both numbers in the deck so you're not guessing.
Yeah, put both. My CFO will ask the exact same thing.

Will do. And the other one I wanted to call out, because it doesn't show up in on-time, is re-optimization. Your dispatchers re-ran routes mid-day about four times as often in Q3 as in Q2. Which, to me, says they actually trust it now. Back in the spring they were doing a lot of it by hand, dragging stops around.

Yeah, that's true. That's mostly because we stopped fighting it. The on-time thing matches what I'm seeing too, for what it's worth. The Tuesday and Wednesday routes in particular, those used to be our worst days and they're fine now. Where it's still rough is the north depot. The routes look good on paper and then the driver sits at a loading dock for twenty-five minutes behind a pallet truck and the whole thing slides.
Is north in the ninety-three eight, or is that dragging it down?
It's in it. North is the lowest of the three, it's around ninety-one, so the other two are carrying it a bit. It's on the second slide.

Yeah, and that's — dock wait time is honestly the hardest thing for the ETA model right now. Kenji, who runs our ML ETA work, his model's error is down from about six minutes to about four point three on average, which is a big improvement, but dense urban stops and dock waits are exactly where it still misses. That's a lot of what Routing v3 is going after. That's the new engine. It's in beta with six fleets right now, GA is November seventeenth, and the beta fleets are seeing about eleven percent fewer miles and on-time going from around ninety-one to ninety-four and a half.
And we're not in that beta.

You're not, no. We kept the beta to smaller fleets on purpose, so if something broke it didn't break a hundred and eighty vans. But you'd be one of the first we move after GA, and I'd want Aisha's north depot to be the first place we turn it on, honestly, because that's where it should help most.
I'd take that.

Okay. Look, the numbers are good. I'm not going to pretend they're not. When I showed our CEO the on-time number he was happy, for about a week. And then the twenty-fourth happened, and that's what he remembers now. So.
Yeah. Understood. Let's go there.

title: The Sep 24 outage and service credit
gist: Jordan and Aisha describe the impact of the Sep 24 ETA outage, about 1,100 customers with wrong windows and a flooded support line; Jordan's main complaint is that the status page lagged 26 minutes and they heard from drivers first. Asher owns it, Sofia offers a 10% credit on one month, and Jordan accepts.

turns.t: So I'll tell you how that morning looked from our side, because I'm not sure you have the full picture. It started a little after seven our time, which is the first wave, that's the busiest hour we have. Drivers are loaded and out. And the ETAs just stopped moving. The app kept showing times, so nobody on our side knew anything was wrong, the times just weren't real. And our customer texts go out off those ETAs. So about eleven hundred customers got a delivery window that was wrong. Some by twenty minutes, some by over an hour. And grocery customers, you know, they're waiting at home for frozen stuff, they planned their morning around it. Our support line got absolutely hammered. We normally take maybe two-fifty calls on a weekday. That day we took something like nine hundred.
Mm.

And honestly, the outage itself, things break, I've run operations long enough, I get it. The part that I'm actually upset about is that we heard about it from our drivers. Not from you. A driver called Aisha and said the app was frozen, and that was the first anyone at Brightside knew. And then your status page said everything was green for, what was it, twenty-six minutes? I had my team refreshing it. Green. So I'm on the phone with my support lead telling her I don't know what's happening, and your page is telling me nothing is happening.

Yeah, it was — so the drivers have a group chat, and by like seven-twenty it was just everyone posting screenshots. Is anyone else's app stuck. Restarting phones. A couple of them started calling customers directly from their personal phones to give them a real time, which, I appreciate the hustle, but we really don't want drivers doing that while they're driving. And I couldn't tell them anything because I didn't know anything. I ended up telling everyone to ignore the app times and just run the stop order, which, that's basically going back to paper.

And then the comps. We comped delivery fees on, I want to say three hundred-something orders, where the window was off by more than an hour or the frozen stuff was soft when it got there. That's our cost, we made that call, I'm not asking you to eat it line by line. But I want you to understand it wasn't just an annoying morning.
No, that's — thank you for laying it out. That's more detail than I had, honestly. I knew it was bad, I didn't know about the comps.

Yeah. So first, I'm sorry. And I want to be specific about what I'm sorry for, because I think you're right about where the real failure was. The ETA service went down for forty-seven minutes, and that's bad, but the part that's genuinely on us and shouldn't have happened is that you found out from your drivers, and that our status page sat green for twenty-six minutes. That's not a technical limitation. Our status page is updated by hand right now, and during the incident the person running it was also the person debugging it. That's a process failure and it's mine to fix, not your problem to work around.
Okay. I appreciate you saying that.

And just quickly on what actually happened, so you've got it. We had a failover in one of our Redis clusters, that's a cache that sits behind the ETA service. That on its own should be a blip. But our dispatch workers started retrying all at once, no backoff, no randomness, so they basically hammered the ETA service until it fell over. And the cached ETAs your drivers were seeing were stale, and nothing in the app told them that. We did a full retro last Friday, the day after. Coming out of it, the workers get proper retry budgets with jitter, the ETA service gets a circuit breaker so it degrades instead of collapsing, and the status page gets updated automatically from our alerts, so a human doesn't have to remember to do it in the middle of a fire. We're also adding a staleness flag, so if an ETA is old, the driver app says so instead of showing a confident wrong number.
Why did it take you that long to even know? Twenty-six minutes, I mean, my drivers knew in five.

Honestly, our alerting was too lenient. The threshold was set so it only paged once errors had been high for a sustained window, which is meant to stop false alarms at three in the morning, but it meant our on-call engineer got paged about six minutes after it started instead of right away. And then it took a while to figure out that the cache failover was the cause and not the symptom. Those thresholds are being tightened this week. That's not an excuse, it's just the honest answer to why.

The staleness flag, yeah. That's actually the one I care about most for the drivers. If it had just said ETA updating or something, they would have known. They wouldn't have been restarting phones for twenty minutes.

Fine. What I'd add is, the status page being automatic is good, but I don't want to be checking a status page. If something hits our fleet, I want a call or a text. Me and Aisha. Before our drivers know.

Yes. That's — I'm writing a customer comms runbook right now, that came out of the retro too, and part of it is exactly that. For accounts like yours there's a named contact list and a pre-approved message we send within, the target is fifteen minutes. I'll add you and Aisha by text, today. And I'll send you the written incident report by Friday, so you have something to hand to your CEO that isn't just me saying sorry on a call.
That would help. He's going to ask me for it.

And then, look, I have to ask. We had nine hundred support calls and eleven hundred customers with bad windows. Some of those we comped. I need to go back with something. What are we talking about on a service credit?

Yeah. So I talked to our finance team before this call, so I'm not making it up on the spot. What we can do is a credit of ten percent of one month, applied to the October invoice. That's — on your current contract that's about twelve hundred dollars. I know that doesn't cover what that morning cost you. It's not meant to pretend it does. It's meant to say we take it seriously.

Yeah. I mean, honestly, I'll take it, and the money isn't really the point. Twelve hundred bucks isn't going to change anything for us. It's more that I need to show we raised it and you responded. So yes, ten percent, October invoice, fine. What actually matters is that it doesn't happen again, and if it does, I hear it from you first.
Understood. That's fair.

And I'd rather you hold us to the second part than the credit, honestly. If there's another incident and you hear about it from a driver before you hear from Sofia, that's the thing I want you to call me about.
Oh, I will.
He will.
Okay. Let's move on before I get worked up again.

title: Live ETA sharing and the Q4 roadmap
gist: Jordan presses on live ETA sharing, which he first asked for in June; Asher explains it is not built, needs about five engineer-weeks, and competes with driver onboarding work, and commits to send the Q4 roadmap with a specific live ETA date by Oct 9.

turns.t: So that's a good segue actually, because the next thing on the list is roadmap, and I know live ETA is the one you want to hear about.

It is. And I'll be honest with you, I'm a little frustrated about it. I asked in June. I was on a call with you, Sofia, I think it was the mid-year check-in, and I said we need a tracking link our customers can open, live driver location, live ETA. And the answer was, it's on the roadmap. And now it's the end of September and I'm asking again.
You did, yeah. That's right.

And the reason I keep pushing is our customers expect it now. They get it from every food delivery app on their phone. Our competitors in two of our metros have it. When someone gets a delivery window of nine to eleven, and it's ten-forty and nothing's showed up, they call us. If they had a link, half those calls go away. That's real money for my support team. And frankly, on the twenty-fourth, if they'd had a live link, at least they'd have seen the van moving.

Yeah. Let me give you the straight version, because I think you've gotten the soft version a couple of times and that's not fair to you. Live ETA sharing is not built. We haven't started it. We've scoped it, it's about five engineer-weeks of work, so it's not a giant project, but it's not nothing. And for Q4 it's competing directly with something else on our list, which is a redesign of the driver app onboarding, which, Aisha, I want to come back to with you, because I think it's relevant to you too. We're finalizing Q4 planning this week. Friday, actually.
Okay, but I've heard, we're figuring out Q4, before. In June it was, we're figuring out Q3.

That's fair. So here's what I'll commit to. By October ninth, so a week from Friday, I will send you the Q4 roadmap, and it'll have a date for live ETA sharing in it. A date, not a quarter. And if the honest answer is that the date is later than you want, I'll tell you that, and I'll tell you why, rather than giving you something vague and letting you find out in January.
A date. Not a range.
A date. If I can't give you one I'll tell you exactly what it depends on, but I'm planning to give you one.
Okay. I'll hold you to that.

Please do. And I'll say one more thing on it, which ties back to the outage. If we'd shipped live ETA in July and then had the twenty-fourth, your customers would have been watching a live link show them a wrong time with total confidence. So the staleness work we're doing, the flag that says this ETA is old, that actually has to land before or with live ETA. It's not a reason to delay. It's just part of doing it right.
Yeah, that's — fine, that makes sense. I don't want a link that lies to people either. That'd be worse than no link.
What does it actually look like, though? Like if I'm a customer. Do I get a text with a link, do I need to download something? Because if it's an app download, nobody's doing that for groceries.

No download. The way we've scoped it, it's a link in the text message you already send, opens in the browser, shows the van on a map once the driver's a few stops away, and a live ETA that updates. Branded as Brightside, not as us. Your customers would never see the word Tandem. And it hides the driver's exact location until they're close, for the driver's privacy, which I think Aisha's drivers would care about.
They would, yeah. Some of them would be really uncomfortable if a customer could watch them sitting on their lunch break.

But can I add one thing from the driver side? The drivers want this too. It's not just customers. Right now when someone's anxious about their order they call the store, the store calls dispatch, dispatch calls the driver. Or the customer just calls the driver directly if they got the number from a previous delivery. The drivers hate it. They're trying to find parking and their phone's ringing with where are you. A link would take a lot of that away.

That's really useful, actually. Can I quote you on that internally? Because the driver-side benefit is a part of the case that I don't think we've been making. We've been pitching it as a customer feature and a support cost thing.
Sure, quote away.
And is it just us asking for this? Because if it's just Brightside, I get that it's harder to prioritize.

No, it's not just you. I can't name names, but we've got a large prospect right now where it's a must-have, not a nice-to-have, and a couple of other customers have asked. So it's not a favor for one account. It's something we need. The question is genuinely sequencing, not whether.
Okay. Good. That's actually reassuring, weirdly. If other people are pushing too, it's more likely to happen.
It is, yeah. You're in good company on this one.

And Jordan, just so it's clear, the roadmap Asher sends on the ninth, I'll put time on the calendar right after so we can walk through it together, rather than you just getting a PDF and having to interpret it.
Sure. That's fine. Just make sure the date's actually in it.
